transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-09-11 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Miguel Santos (Redwood CSM); Daniel Ortiz (Mistral CISO), Sana Malik (Eng Manager), Ibrahim Khan (DevOps), Lucie Dupont (QA)
Shared artifacts: pen-test report (Mistral-PT-2025-08.pdf), vuln-prio-spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.example.com/mistral/vuln-prio), SOC2 summary (link: https://redwood.example.com/soc2/mistral)

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We'll keep this to about 50 minutes. Quick intros? I think we all know each other but quick round robin.
[00:15] Daniel Ortiz: Yeah this is Daniel, CISO at Mistral. Appreciate you setting this up. We just got the final pen-test and wanted to go through triage — particularly the critical/high surface area.
[00:25] Priya Nair: Hi all, Priya from Redwood, I'll walk through mapping findings to our runtime and ops model. Quick note: some automated transcripts swap cloud names — so if you see "big cloud" in the notes it's probably BigCloudAI.
[00:40] Sana Malik: Sana here. We'll focus on patch cadence and what touches our SDLC.
[00:45] Ibrahim Khan: Ibrahim, DevOps. I'll own any patch windows and retest runs.
[00:50] Miguel Santos: Miguel from CS. I'll coordinate the artifacts and follow-ups.
[00:55] Lucie Dupont: Lucie, QA. I'll help validate fixes in pre-prod.

Summary / High level
[01:10] Alex Chen: Quick agenda: 1) Align on top 5 critical findings from the pen test; 2) discuss remediation and who touches Redwood infra vs Mistral infra; 3) confirm patching cadence & blackout windows; 4) validation plan and retest timeline; 5) open items on SOC2/KMS/encryption.

Findings review
[02:00] Daniel Ortiz: We categorized 23 findings: 3 critical, 7 high, rest medium/low. The critical ones are: unauthenticated object store S3 bucket listing (false-positive?), exposed debug endpoint in a container, and a privilege escalation vector via third-party dependency.
[02:22] Priya Nair: For the object store, can you confirm whether that bucket is managed by Redwood dedicated capacity or is in your customer-owned aws account?
[02:35] Ibrahim Khan: That's in our AWS account but it's mounted as a cache volume for the batch jobs that talk to Redwood Dedicated. So there's a shared surface area. We did restrict ACLs but the pen tester found list permissions broadly.
[02:50] Priya Nair: Okay that helps. From Redwood's side, we advise locking to bucket policy + VPC gateway endpoints; for Dedicated we also recommend short-lived credentials via STS and no long-lived keys in task definitions. We'll attach a remediation playbook.
[03:12] Alex Chen: Note: we'll include a sample IAM policy and an example STS assume role snippet in the doc we send.

Timestamped transcript (excerpted)
[04:00] Daniel Ortiz: About the exposed debug endpoint — that was a container we left on for a jenkins job ages ago, but it's in the prod cluster. The tester hit /debug and was able to get stack traces.
[04:18] Priya Nair: Is that in Redwood-managed runtime or in your private deployment?
[04:23] Daniel Ortiz: It's in our private deployment — on-prem. We patched it after the test but want to talk cadence to avoid drift.
[04:30] Alex Chen: Good. For private deployments we recommend a quarterly baseline configuration scan plus pre-prod hardening checks before every major rollout. That pairs with our recommended secure SDLC gating: automated dependency scanning, infra-as-code scans, and RBAC review.
[04:50] Sana Malik: On SDLC we currently run Snyk on PRs for code deps but not on container base images. Anything Redwood recommends for images?
[04:59] Priya Nair: Yes we suggest image scanning on build pipelines (Clair/Trivy) and a separate image SBOM export stored in your artifact repo. We can provide example CI steps.

[06:10] Ibrahim Khan: The third critical item was a privilege escalation via a third-party library in our inference client — CVE-2024-xxxx. We did a hotfix but it's a library used in multiple services.
[06:25] Miguel Santos: Did the tester show exploitability?
[06:28] Daniel Ortiz: Yes they demonstrated a local exploit that could lead to remote code execution in a specific config. We mitigated by upgrading to patched version but need to track usages across environments.
[06:40] Priya Nair: We'll help with an SBOM sweep against services we know integrate with Redwood SDKs and provide a suggested remediation window. Typical approach: patch in canary, monitor logs for anomalies, then schedule full rollout.

Patching cadence discussion
[07:15] Alex Chen: Ibrahim — what's your current patch window and blackout dates?
[07:22] Ibrahim Khan: We have weekly maintenance windows Wednesday 02:00-04:00 UTC and a monthly major maintenance on first Saturday 01:00-05:00 UTC. Blackout windows: end-of-quarter deploy freeze.
[07:38] Alex Chen: For high severity infra patches we recommend immediate canary outside blackout if possible, otherwise next weekly window. For Dedicated customers, Redwood can coordinate to hold capacity for warm failover to reduce customer-side downtime.
[07:55] Daniel Ortiz: If Redwood can provide a warm failover or short-term instance routing we might accept more frequent critical patches.
[08:02] Priya Nair: We can—depends on plan (Dedicated vs Private). For Private on-prem we provide runbooks but not direct failover.

RBAC / SSO / Audit logging
[09:00] Sana Malik: We want to tighten RBAC in our console and audit trails. Are there built-in audit exports from Redwood that we can ship to our SIEM?
[09:12] Priya Nair: Yes, Redwood exposes per-token and per-request audit logs; you can forward to CloudWatch/Stackdriver or to your SIEM via a webhook. We'll provide the format spec. Note: tokens are redacted and we include request context and route/model used.
[09:30] Lucie Dupont: Is there a way to get immutable logs for compliance?
[09:36] Miguel Santos: We support log forwarding to an S3 bucket with write-once lifecycle policy, or your SIEM can enforce immutability. We'll include recommendations for retention and tamper evidence.

Encryption / KMS / Data residency
[10:20] Alex Chen: Quick run on encryption: data at rest is encrypted using customer-managed KMS for Dedicated and Private; hosted uses Redwood-managed KMS but we offer bring-your-own-key for enterprise. For data residency we can pin regions for hosting and provide VPC endpoints.
[10:40] Daniel Ortiz: Mistral needs keys in our HSM for a few regulated workloads. Can Redwood integrate with on-prem HSM or external KMS?
[10:48] Priya Nair: For Private yes; we have integrations for vault/HSM via PKCS#11 and can use external KMS for key wrapping. For Dedicated we support BYOK via Cloud KMS integrations. We'll attach the KMS integration runbook.

Validation and retest plan
[11:30] Alex Chen: Proposed retest plan: prioritize top-5 findings (the 3 critical + 2 high exploitable ones), remediate, then schedule retest with the pen test vendor. Redwood can assist with a pre-retest checklist and environment snapshots. Target retest in 10 business days after fixes.
[11:50] Daniel Ortiz: That timeline sounds OK if we get the remediation playbook today.
[12:00] Priya Nair: We'll send the playbook + IAM templates + SBOM sweep results. Also we'll include a mapping of who owns each remediations — Redwood vs Mistral.

Questions / Clarifications raised during call
[12:30] Lucie Dupont: Quick Q: for our pre-prod validation, can Redwood spin a test harness or do we need to run internal QA only?
[12:40] Priya Nair: We can provide a lightweight harness that exercises common routes and memory/kv cache behaviors — it's not a penetration test harness but helps validate behavior. Link to harness: https://redwood.example.com/mistral/harness
[12:55] Lucie Dupont: Great.

[13:30] Ibrahim Khan: One more — audit logging granularity: can we get per-token cost breakdown in the audit log to tie spikes to specific requests?
[13:40] Miguel Santos: Yes, the token-level breakdown is part of our observability exports; we can include it in the audit stream but note that sensitive prompt content is redacted by default.

Tradeoffs and objections
[14:30] Daniel Ortiz: We debated whether to maintain Dedicated vs move fully to Private for sensitive workloads. Private reduces shared infra risk but increases operational burden.
[14:42] Alex Chen: Exactly — Dedicated gives isolation at the node/network layer with Redwood-managed operations; Private gives you full control for HSM/KMS and network. We can create a decision checklist that weighs cost, compliance, and ops.

Artifacts and follow-ups mentioned
[15:20] Miguel Santos: I'll upload the prioritized vuln spreadsheet to the secure share and mark Redwood-owned vs Mistral-owned items. Link will be posted in the follow-up note.
[15:34] Alex Chen: We'll also send a SOC2 artifact bundle (redacted) and our architecture diagram.

Closing and recap
[16:00] Alex Chen: Recap — Redwood action: send SOC2 + arch diagram, send remediation playbook & IAM snippets, provide SBOM sweep and harness link. Mistral action: confirm patch windows and SBOM list. Target retest week of 2025-09-22.
[16:20] Daniel Ortiz: Sounds good. We also want a brief runbook for immediate containment if an exploit is observed in the wild.
[16:28] Priya Nair: We'll include a containment checklist: revoke tokens, rotate STS roles, isolate nodes, and instructions for rehydrating from backup.

Transcript notes / rough transcript quirks: some names autocorrected (e.g., "Priya" sometimes shows as "Priam"), technical terms like KV cache sometimes transcribed as "K-V cash", and proper nouns like HSM were occasionally lowercased.

[20:00] Daniel Ortiz: (offhand) can you also share any recent regression alerts tied to prompt evals? We had a false positive last month where an eval caught a policy drift.
[20:12] Alex Chen: We can share quality/regression alert templates — Redwood Optimize hooks into evals and can tie them to deployments to trigger rollbacks.

[22:00] Sana Malik: For the dependency that was used across services, do you have recommended tools to discover transitive usage?
[22:10] Priya Nair: We suggest SBOM + call-graph analysis and a runtime dependency tracer. We'll include an example script that parses SBOMs and greps for the vulnerable artifact.

[30:45] Ibrahim Khan: One blocker — change freeze next month (end of quarter). If fixes are high risk we may need to do an emergency patch; any guidelines on emergency rollouts?
[31:00] Alex Chen: Emergency rollouts: notify Redwood SRE, attach a rollback plan, run canary on isolated nodes, coordinate DB migrations off-line if any. We'll provide a template for emergency change notes.

[40:10] Lucie Dupont: QA question: when we validate the fix, should we use the same test vectors the pen tester used?
[40:18] Miguel Santos: Ideally yes, but you'll need permission from the pentest vendor. Redwood can run a blackbox verification if you prefer to avoid sharing vendor tooling.

[46:00] Daniel Ortiz: Final ask: for audit/compliance we'll need a one-page attestation that the critical findings were remediated and dates. Can Redwood provide that?
[46:12] Priya Nair: Yes, after retest we can provide an attestation letter that lists findings and remediation status, suitable for SOC/ISO auditors. We'll include contact for compliance escalation.

[50:00] Alex Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with notes and the links. Miguel will own the secure share upload.
[50:10] Miguel Santos: Noted. Thanks.
[50:20] Daniel Ortiz: Thanks all. Meeting end.
additional_notes: This transcript is an exported Fireflies-style artifact. Some transcription errors expected. Shared links are placeholders to secure-share locations. Pen tester vendor is listed in the report as RedCrow Security. Retest target tentative week of 2025-09-22.
